plan: A: Nuxt frontend + existing Flask backend on Vercel Services
notes: Phase 1 runs Nuxt with ssr: false (SPA). Browser calls /api/* as today, so vercel.json rewrites and Flask stay the same.
Phase 2 (optional) turns on SSR/hybrid for some pages. Server-side fetches cannot use relative /api, so they need a Vercel service binding URL.
Only set passes to true after running every step in that feature and seeing it work.
Backend tests: cd backend && pytest. They must stay green for every feature.

Phase 3 adds a game detail page at /games/[id]. Game info (name, genres, rating, cover, summary) comes from the IGDB API; every store price comes from CheapShark. id is the CheapShark gameID. Flask calls both APIs, so IGDB credentials never reach the browser.

Phases 4-9 make the search page more engaging: filters and sorting (4), a landing page with top titles and a biggest-discount sidebar (5), historical-low badges (6), wishlist and recently viewed (7), email price alerts (8), discovery: header quick search, similar games, browse by genre (9).

Filters and sorting use CheapShark GET /deals (title, lowerPrice, upperPrice, storeID, onSale, metacritic, steamRating, sortBy, desc, pageNumber, pageSize<=60; total pages in the X-Total-Page-Count response header). /deals returns one row per store, so the backend keeps only the cheapest row per gameID. Its title filter is a substring match ('portal' also returns 'SPORTAL'), so a text search with the default 'Relevance' sort keeps the current /games?title search and applies the filters to those results.

CheapShark prices are USD. Price filters typed in THB/EUR are converted to USD before calling CheapShark, then results are checked again after conversion so every shown price is inside the range the user typed.

Landing page lists (top rated, new, free, biggest discounts) are the same for every visitor: cache raw CheapShark /deals responses in memory for 15 min and send Cache-Control so the Vercel CDN can cache /api responses. In-memory cache is per serverless instance, so it only reduces load, it is not shared.

Wishlist and recently viewed are stored in the browser (localStorage), no accounts. Pages /wishlist and /browse use query strings (/browse?genre=12), not dynamic paths, so they can be prerendered like /about and need no vercel.json change.

Price alerts use CheapShark GET /alerts?action=set&email=&gameID=&price= (price in USD). CheapShark sends the emails, so the user's email address leaves our server; the form must say so. The browser POSTs to Flask so the email is not in our URLs or access logs.

Alert rate limits per IP per hour (owner's choice, 2026-11-16): set alert 10, manage email 5, counted separately (config.ALERTS_LIMITS). alert-01 says 'e.g. more than 5'; the final value for setting alerts is 10.

Phase 10 fixes card images. CheapShark only gives a small landscape 'thumb' (Steam capsule 231x87 or a store image). Portrait art comes from Steam's library_600x900.jpg built from steamAppID (no API call); it returns 404 for some new games (hashed asset paths) and games not on Steam have no steamAppID, so the browser falls back to the landscape thumb, shown whole (object-contain) over a blurred copy instead of cropped. Detail page screenshots come from IGDB (screenshots.image_id, added to the existing find_game query, no extra request): t_screenshot_big (889x500) in the strip, t_1080p in the full view.

features.description: Replace the Vite + Vue app in frontend/ with a Nuxt app that has ssr: false

Run npm run dev and see the app at http://localhost:3000

Find the IGDB game by CheapShark's steamAppID first (external_games, Steam source, uid = steamAppID); if there is no steamAppID or no match, search by title and take the best match
Fetch fields: name, genres.name, rating, rating_count, aggregated_rating, cover.image_id, summary, first_release_date
Raise UpstreamError when IGDB fails; return None when no game matches
Add pytest tests with mocked HTTP: token caching, Steam match, title fallback, no match, IGDB error

features.description: Backend: GET /api/deals with filters, sorting and paging

main: Frontend calls /api/deals?q=portal&currency=THB&minPrice=100&maxPrice=500&sort=newest&page=0

Response is { results[], page, totalPages, currency }; each result has the /api/search fields plus retailPrice, savings, steamRating, metacriticScore, releaseDate; one result per game, the cheapest store
alternate: No q: returns deals for all games matching the filters (e.g. every game under 5 USD, newest first)
q with sort=relevance (the default when q is set): uses the current /games?title search and applies the filters to its results; totalPages is 1
Only one of minPrice/maxPrice given: the other side is open
maxPrice=0: only games that are free right now
Same request again within 15 min: served from the in-memory cache, no CheapShark call
error: minPrice > maxPrice, negative price, unknown sort, page < 0, non-numeric value: 400 JSON with a message naming the bad parameter
Unknown currency: same 400 as /api/search
CheapShark down or timeout: same 502 JSON as /api/search, never a 500 traceback

steps: Add cheapshark.list_deals(params) that calls GET /deals and returns (rows, totalPages); http.py needs a way to read the X-Total-Page-Count header (default totalPages 1 when it is missing)
Cache list_deals results in memory for 15 min keyed by the sorted USD params; cap the cache (e.g. 200 entries, drop the oldest)
Add services/deals.py: validate params, map sort (relevance, deal, price, savings, rating, reviews, newest) to CheapShark sortBy, convert minPrice/maxPrice to USD, pageSize 30
Keep only the cheapest row per gameID; convert prices with the exchange rate; drop rows outside the requested range after conversion
sort=relevance with q: reuse search_prices and filter its results locally (price range, stores, onSale)
Optional filters: stores=1,7 (storeID list), onSale=1, minRating=80 (Steam rating percent)
Add route routes/deals.py mapping errors to 400/502 like search.py
Add tests with CheapShark mocked: each sort mapping, currency conversion of the price bounds, dedupe per gameID, range check after conversion, relevance path, cache hit, every 400 case, 502
cd backend && pytest stays green
Update README endpoint list
